title: The Joy of True Mental Effort
text:
This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. 

 This past week, my colleague Lila Shroff recounted her experience at a “drunk deriving” party in San Francisco. The event is exactly what it sounds like: libations and collaborative attempts to solve math and logic problems. “The winning team will be the one with the highest combined blood-alcohol levels and exam score,” Lila writes.

 In Lila’s delightful story, she spends time with the people who remain devoted to the joy of doing math, even as AI transforms the field. Working with numbers means something different to each mathematician she speaks with—some delight in the purity of knowing there’s one right answer; for others, it’s the adrenaline rush of solving a problem. But one idea she returns to throughout the story is the togetherness of something like the drunk-deriving party. That kind of collaboration will become even more important as math evolves and becomes more accessible to the public, Lila writes. “Maybe the future is to be found in the drunk part of the drunk-math party—not in the encouragement of drunkenness itself, but in the partnership that I encounter when I ask my teammates for help.”

 Today’s newsletter explores how to fully engage the brain, and the value of doing that alongside other people.
